24-860 CARTER V. UNITED STATES
DECISION BELOW: 2024 WL 5339852
CONSOLIDATED FOR ONE HOUR ORAL ARGUMENT WITH 24-820.
CERT. GRANTED 6/6/2025
QUESTION PRESENTED:
Congress empowered district courts to reduce sentences of federal prisoners for
"extraordinary and compelling reasons." Congress did not define the terms
"extraordinary and compelling" but instead expressly delegated to the United States
Sentencing Commission the authority to describe what types of circumstances qualify.
Exercising that authority, the Sentencing Commission adopted a provision, Section
1B1.13(b)(6), that permits district courts to consider a sentence reduction where, among
other things, the defendant has served at least ten years of an unusually long sentence
and a nonretroactive change in law produces a "gross disparity" between that sentence
and the one likely to be imposed at the time of the motion. The Courts of Appeals are
divided on the question presented here:
Whether the Sentencing Commission acted within its expressly delegated
authority by permitting district courts to consider, in narrowly cabined circumstances, a
nonretroactive change in law in determining whether "extraordinary and compelling
reasons" warrant a sentence reduction.
LOWER COURT CASE NUMBER: 24-1115
